name: Three-point lighting
summary: A key light, a fill light and a back light on one subject, so that the face is modelled and stands out from the ground.
how: Set the key light 30 to 45 degrees off the camera axis and above eye level.
Set the fill on the other side at 1/4 to 1/2 of the key.
Put the back light behind the subject, so that a thin rim of light separates hair and shoulders from the ground.

origin.note: In the 1920s Hollywood cameramen light stars with a key, a fill and a back light; in the 1930s the method is the studio standard.

adoptions.via: George Hurrell and other studio portraitists bring key, fill and back light to portraits for film and fashion magazines.
Creators light skin with a soft key at the window, a fill and a ring light, which gives the dewy sheen.

sources.title: Kristin Thompson, David Bordwell and Janet Staiger, The Classical Hollywood Cinema (1985)
